#!/bin/bash
# Flux job script translated from Slurm

#flux: -q gpu
#flux: -N 1
#flux: -n 1
#flux: -t 01:30:00

# The original script specified separate output and error files.
# Flux merges stderr with stdout by default when a single output file is specified.
#flux: -o with_gpu.out

# CRITICAL: The Slurm GPU request '--gres=gpu:1' has been OMITTED.
# There is no standard Flux directive to request GPUs. This functionality is highly site-specific.
# This job is being submitted to the 'gpu' queue, which is assumed to provide the necessary GPU resources.
# If the queue does not provide a GPU, the job will FAIL.
# #SBATCH --gres=gpu:1

# The Slurm '--gres-flags=enforce-binding' directive has no direct equivalent in Flux and is omitted.
# Flux's default resource binding is generally sufficient.

# Load CUDA module
module load cuda/12.2.2  gcc/10.2   


nvidia-smi 

# Compile CUDA program and run
#nvcc -arch sm_20 vecadd.cu -o vecadd

# The commands are run directly. As this is a single-task job, 'flux run' is not necessary.
nvcc -O2 -std=c++11 hw4.cu -o a.out
nvprof ./a.out
nsys profile ./a.out

issues: CRITICAL: As noted in the script's comments, the original Slurm request for a GPU (`--gres=gpu:1`) was omitted. While the translated script is syntactically valid, it is functionally incorrect. The script loads a CUDA module, compiles and runs CUDA code, and calls `nvidia-smi`, all of which confirm a GPU is essential. The job will almost certainly fail at runtime because it will not be allocated a GPU unless the 'gpu' queue guarantees it.

The script compiles the application (`nvcc ...`) and then immediately runs it within the same job. This is a common pattern for development and testing but is not ideal for production, as compilation can be time-consuming and is better done once, interactively or in a separate build job.

#!/bin/bash
#!/bin/bash

# Request a GPU partition node and access to 1 GPU
#SBATCH -p gpu --gres=gpu:1 --gres-flags=enforce-binding

# Ensures all allocated cores are on the same node
#SBATCH -N 1

# Request 1 CPU core
#SBATCH -n 1

#SBATCH -t 01:30:00
#SBATCH -o with_gpu.out
#SBATCH -e with_gpu.err

# Load CUDA module
module load cuda/12.2.2  gcc/10.2   


nvidia-smi 

# Compile CUDA program and run
#nvcc -arch sm_20 vecadd.cu -o vecadd
nvcc -O2 -std=c++11 hw4.cu -o a.out
nvprof ./a.out
nsys profile ./a.out
